_comment: Calage sidecar for the Wayfinders 'meshes' jalon. Tells Rune how this iso-render PNG registers onto a Godot IsoBoard at J5. Produced by Mira 2026-05-22. Regeneratable -- do not hand-edit.

schema._doc: Calage sidecar schema v2 (2026-05-22b). v1 shipped a flat separable 'render_scale' (px/m on X and Y independently) -- that is INVALID for an iso render and was removed. v2 ships the exact iso projection under 'iso_projection.world_to_pixel_projection'. Consumers MUST use that block.
consume: iso_projection.world_to_pixel_projection.origin_px    -- px of the SW reference corner
removed_in_v2: render_scale (flat separable px/m -- mathematically wrong for iso)

iso_projection.note: Render canvas is 2:1 (w = 2*h). The PNG is a true iso view of a flat extruded slab -- the silhouette IS the land/district outline. world_to_pixel_projection below is the EXACT transform; do NOT use a flat px/m scale.

world_to_pixel_projection._doc: EXACT world(metres)->pixel(this PNG) transform for a ground-level point. The PNG is a 2:1 iso render: pixelX is NOT separable from worldY. Use world_to_pixel (the 2x3 affine) OR the equivalent iso_basis/origin form below -- they are identical. Apply to a point on the flat ground plane (reference_plane below).

reference_plane.note: POIs register on the flat ground plane Z=0, NOT on the extruded land crest. The mesh extrusion (LAND_HEIGHT) raises the visible silhouette top, but city/POI world coordinates are 2D ground coordinates -- project them at Z=0.

world_to_pixel_projection.formula: pixelX = (worldX - anchorX)*iso_basis_x[0] + (worldY - anchorY)*iso_basis_y[0] + origin_px[0] ; pixelY = (worldX - anchorX)*iso_basis_x[1] + (worldY - anchorY)*iso_basis_y[1] + origin_px[1]

iso_basis_x._doc: Pixel displacement (dx, dy) for +1 metre EAST (world +X).

iso_basis_y._doc: Pixel displacement (dx, dy) for +1 metre NORTH (world +Y).

origin_px._doc: Pixel where the world reference point (the SW corner of the frame: worldX=anchorX, worldY=anchorY) lands on the PNG. May be slightly negative -- CAM_ORTHO_SCALE keeps a 10% margin, so the plane does not touch the canvas edge.

world_to_pixel._doc: Equivalent 2x3 affine matrix applied to absolute world coords: [pixelX, pixelY]^T = M . [worldX, worldY, 1]^T. Row-major: [[m00,m01,m02],[m10,m11,m12]].

control_point._doc: Verified pin for Rune's xUnit test. This world point feeds through the projection to exactly this pixel. The frame CENTRE is used because it is margin-independent: it always lands at the PNG centre.

_derivation.note: Mirrors map_terrain_mesh_script.py: PLANE_WIDTH, CAM_ORTHO_SCALE = PLANE_WIDTH*1.10, CAM_ROT_X=60, CAM_ROT_Z=45, _pixel_to_world centred+Y-flipped plane.

world_frame_m.anchor_note: SW corner of the rendered world frame, in world meters (world.yaml convention: origin SW, X east, Y north).

ground_scale.note: Source-bitmap density only (provenance). NOT a render transform -- use iso_projection.world_to_pixel_projection to place anything on the PNG.

godot_placement.note: eM backdrop. Wire as IsoBoard.BackgroundTexturePath; Sprite2D Centered=false, top-left at the board origin. Cities pin as POIs via city.position (world meters, ground Z=0) -> render pixels using iso_projection.world_to_pixel_projection (NOT a flat px/m scale -- the render is isometric). Halfgate placeholder (92000,38000) is tunable until this coastline render is signed off (Varn spec section 7).
